reason: Confirmed on the source and by driving the page. b.css:152 declares .b-item with no transition, and render-b.js:233 writes item.style.top inside the click handler, so the computed transition on the edited item is 'all 0s'. Sampling offsetTop every frame after a week-earlier press gives 322 at 0ms and 224 at 2ms with no intermediate value: a hard cut. The whole motion inventory of the approach room is five colour transitions at 0.14s (.b-switch border-color, .b-act border+background, .b-grab background, .b-step background, .b-seg button background+color) and no keyframes anywhere; the seat named three of the five, which is imprecise but does not change the substance. Nothing in this master moves position, ever. Transitioning top is the right call for this direction, not a taste preference. Vertical position IS the quantity here (daysFromToday x px, lock.md), so animating position is not decorating a state change, it is rendering the change of the quantity itself. Under 'motion is physics rather than personality' (shell.css:40) that is the strongest case for motion in the whole master: it carries information, not character. The ladder already permits it exactly, so this needs no amendment. 0.22s is a declared duration (--t-slow) and cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) is the one declared easing, which is precisely what audit.mjs:207-220 validates against. 0.22s is the correct rung rather than 0.14s: a seven-day press at desk px=14 travels 98px, and the ease-out-quint is 99% arrived by ~170ms, so it reads as a thing settling rather than sliding. The curve never overshoots, so 'nothing bounces, nothing floats idly' holds. top rather than transform is also correct and should not be 'improved' into transform: both gates measure offsetTop (interaction-check.mjs:161 proportionality, :288 the stepper assertion), and animating transform would make the drawn position disagree with the measured position mid-flight. I verified the fix does not break either gate. Injecting the rule and re-running the existing gate shape (click, waitForTimeout(200), read) still gives the full 98px delta, so 'the stepper moves the edited item nearer' and 'both readouts agree' still pass; under emulated reduced motion the longest transition on the page is still 0.001s, so shell.css:202-208 covers the new property and interaction-check.mjs:457 still passes. Six frames of initial-paint sampling show no slide on load, because tops are inline style attributes set before insertion. The counting number is also right rather than decoration, for the same reason and with one condition. lock.md requires distances be named in words as well as drawn, and interaction-check.mjs:309-310 already asserts both readouts agree; if the row travels for 0.22s while the numeral snaps at 0ms, the instrument contradicts itself for the whole duration, which is a worse defect than the jump cut. What would make it decoration is the fix's actual wording, 'count the figure from its old value to its new one', which is a second independent tween and on a large jump reads as a slot-machine roll. Where it stops being decoration is sampling the numeral from the row's real animated position each frame, so the figure is a readout of where the thing is rather than a separate animation of a separate thing. Three corrections to the fix as written: the requestAnimationFrame is unnecessary and harmful, the 80ms assertion is too thin, and .b-stepRead is a third readout the fix forgets.
sharpenedFix: 1. b.css, on .b-item (line 152): add `transition: top var(--t-slow) var(--ease);` using the tokens rather than literals, so the audit ladder stays the single source. Leave it unscoped: nothing writes top after first paint (no resize listener; tops are inline style attributes set before insertion, verified over six frames), and the console's spacing switch flips position to relative with `top: auto !important`, which is not interpolable, so that toggle stays a cut and never smears. 2. render-b.js move(): do NOT wrap the write in requestAnimationFrame. The element already has a resolved computed top, so the inline write transitions natively (verified: 322 -> 292 -> 267 -> 250 -> 239 -> 233 -> 229 -> 227 -> 225 -> 224, settled by ~172ms). Deferring it into rAF only decouples the mutation from the click handler and puts the two settled-state assertions at interaction-check.mjs:303 and :310 into a race for no gain. 3. Do not tween the number separately. On each frame until transitionend, set both readouts from the row's real position: `Math.round(item.offsetTop / px)` into .b-away, and the same figure into .b-stepRead, then write the authoritative `current` once on transitionend so the figure lands exactly on the integer (transitionend still fires under reduced motion at 0.001s, so the collapsed path stays correct). Sampling rather than tweening also fixes the one-day case by construction: a 14px move flips one integer once, mid-slide, instead of stretching a single value change across thirteen frames as a delayed snap. Both figures are already tabular (b.css:161 and :436), so the column will not jitter. Keep .b-away a bare number, per the existing comment at render-b.js:234-236. 4. interaction-check.mjs: bump the `waitForTimeout(200)` at line 294 to 260 so the settled assertions read a landed value rather than a 99.99%-landed one. Add a structural assertion that .b-item's computed transitionProperty includes top with duration 0.22s and easing exactly cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) — structural beats timing. Add at most one mid-flight sample, and take it on the week-earlier press at 40-60ms, not at 80ms: I measured that at 80ms a one-day move sits at 40 of an end of 42, which is two pixels of headroom, and by 120ms it has already landed, so an 80ms assertion on a small move is a flake waiting to happen. At 40ms the same move reads 22 against an end of 28.
